turns.prompt_text: I have a good 10k floating around, I would like to diversify my portfolio on fidelity.com, I could go with a moderately high-risk allocation
turns.response_html:
For a "moderately high-risk" portfolio (often termed "Growth" or "Aggressive Growth"), the goal is typically long-term capital appreciation. This usually involves tolerating higher volatility in exchange for potentially greater returns over time.

Investors with this profile often lean toward an asset allocation of roughly 70–85% stocks (equities) and 15–30% bonds (fixed income).

To satisfy your preference for gathering perspectives from a variety of sources and continents, you might consider a "Core and Satellite" approach. This allows you to anchor the portfolio with a broad market index while using the remaining funds to target specific regions, sectors, or strategies.

Here is a breakdown of how a $10k diversified portfolio on Fidelity could be structured to fit this profile.

1. The Core: Broad Market Exposure (40–50%)

This portion captures the "wisdom of the crowd" by tracking the largest companies in the U.S. It provides a stable foundation.

  • Fidelity 500 Index Fund (FXAIX): Tracks the S&P 500. It is extremely low-cost and captures the performance of large U.S. companies.
  • Alternative: Fidelity Total Market Index Fund (FSKAX) if you want to include smaller U.S. companies and trades (manufacturers, builders, etc.) that aren't in the S&P 500.

2. Global Perspectives: International & Emerging Markets (20–30%)

To align with your interest in "different continents" and "different ways of life," this allocation exposes you to economies outside the U.S., including developing nations.

  • Fidelity Total International Index Fund (FTIHX): Covers both developed markets (like Europe and Japan) and emerging markets.
  • Fidelity Emerging Markets Fund (FEMKX): Focuses specifically on developing economies (e.g., India, Brazil, Southeast Asia). This is higher risk but taps into markets with different demographics and growth trajectories than the West.

3. "High Conviction" Growth: Sectors & Innovation (10–20%)

This slice targets companies with a "natural knack" for innovation—often in technology or specific sectors that drive change. This is the highest-risk portion of the equity bucket.

  • Fidelity Blue Chip Growth Fund (FBGRX): Actively managed; focuses on companies with high growth potential (often tech-heavy).
  • Fidelity Select Technology (FSPTX): A pure sector fund. It is volatile but historically has offered high growth during tech booms.
  • Fidelity Contrafund (FCNTX): A famous fund managed by Will Danoff, known for a contrarian perspective—investing in companies he believes are undervalued or misunderstood by the general market.

4. Aggressive Income: Bonds (10–15%)

In a moderately high-risk portfolio, even the "safe" money often takes a little more risk to generate higher yield.

  • Fidelity High Income Fund (SPHIX): Invests in "junk bonds" (lower credit quality corporate debt). These behave somewhat like stocks and offer higher payouts than government bonds.
  • Fidelity Floating Rate High Income (FFRHX): Invests in loans with floating interest rates, which can offer protection if interest rates vary.

Example Allocation for $10,000

This is a hypothetical split to illustrate a "Growth" profile:

AllocationFund IdeaAmountRole
40%FXAIX (S&P 500)$4,000Stability & US Large Cap
20%FTIHX (Intl Index)$2,000Global Diversification
20%FBGRX (Blue Chip Growth)$2,000Aggressive Growth
10%FEMKX (Emerging Mkts)$1,000High Risk/Reward Intl
10%SPHIX (High Income Bond)$1,000Income with moderate risk

Alternative: The "One-Fund" Solution

If you prefer a professional manager to adjust these perspectives for you, Fidelity offers "Asset Manager" funds that maintain a specific risk profile automatically.

  • Fidelity Asset Manager 70% (FASGX): Automatically holds ~70% stocks and ~30% bonds/short-term investments.
  • Fidelity Asset Manager 85% (FAMRX): Automatically holds ~85% stocks and ~15% bonds (more aggressive).
